haiku-low.q1: They sign in normally. The linked Google sub is trusted alone, and email and email_verified are ignored, so the Gmail change has no effect.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter that account's correct password on the confirm page. Only then is the link inserted, the pending record deleted, and a session started.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5, the account locks for 15 minutes, and the pending link is discarded and the user returns to login. Non-locking failures keep the original 10-minute expiry.
haiku-low.q4: If verified and no user matches, a new user is created with the lowercased email and NULL password, linked, and signed in. If not verified, the user returns to login with a message and nothing is created.
haiku-low.q5: Both cases fail. After 12 minutes the state has expired, and a repeated callback finds it already consumed by GETDEL. Either way the user sees an error page and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q6: It is the same session as password login: a new sessions row and a new sid cookie. Any old sessions row named by the existing sid cookie is deleted.
haiku-low.q7: Neither is required. The settings link only inserts a row, with no password or email check. If the Google account is linked to another user, the user sees a refusal and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis under g:state:<state>, with the browser holding a g_flow cookie. The callback removes them with one GETDEL, or the 600-second TTL removes them if the user never returns.
haiku-low.q9: Redis key g:pending:<token> holds target_user_id, sub and next. The browser holds it as the g_pending cookie. Correct password, lockout, Cancel or the 600-second expiry deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In PostgreSQL table user_google_accounts. PRIMARY KEY on user_id and UNIQUE on google_sub enforce one Google account per user and one user per Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user is redirected to the start with "We couldn't complete sign-in with Google. Please try again." Nothing changes. There is no retry, because the state is already used.
haiku-low.q12: The origin is stored in Redis at start, not read from the callback URL. The callback checks state and the g_flow cookie, and for settings requires the session user to equal the recorded user_id.

sonnet.q1: They sign in normally. A linked sub is trusted on its own; the email and email_verified are ignored, so the changed Gmail address has no effect and they get a session via start_session.
sonnet.q2: They must enter the existing account's password on the confirm page (after a g:pending record is saved and the g_pending cookie set). Only if the account has no other Google account linked and has a password; a correct password inserts the link, then start_session creates the session.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins; at 5, locked_until = now + 15 min and failed_logins resets to 0. On lockout the pending record is deleted, g_pending cleared, and the user is sent to the login page (Account temporarily locked); the link is thrown away. Wrong passwords that don't lock leave the pending record with its original expiry.
sonnet.q4: Verified email with no matching user: in one transaction a new user is created with Google's lowercased email, NULL password_hash and email_verified_at now, plus the link, then start_session. If email_verified is not true: back to login with 'Google email not verified, use email and password'; nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: Error page, nothing changes. At 12 minutes the g:state record (TTL 600 s) has expired; on a second load it was already consumed by GETDEL. Either way state is unknown/expired/used, so no session and no DB change.
sonnet.q6: The same ordinary session as password login: start_session deletes the old sessions row if a sid cookie came in, inserts a new sessions row, sets a new sid cookie, and redirects to next or /home. No new session type.
sonnet.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required (emails need not match); only a session and CSRF protection. If the Google account (sub) is linked to another user: back to settings saying that Google account is linked to someone else; nothing changes.
sonnet.q8: In Redis under g:state:<state> (holding code_verifier, nonce, origin, next, user_id for settings, and a browser token matching the g_flow cookie), TTL 600 s. The callback's atomic GETDEL deletes it (and clears g_flow); if the user never returns, the TTL removes it.
sonnet.q9: In Redis at g:pending:<token> holding target_user_id, sub and next (no email, no tokens). The browser refers to it via the g_pending cookie (random secret, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, path /auth/google). Deleted on correct password, lockout, Cancel, and expiry (TTL 600 s, not extended by wrong passwords).
sonnet.q10: In PostgreSQL table user_google_accounts (user_id, google_sub, linked_at). PRIMARY KEY on user_id gives one Google account per user; UNIQUE on google_sub gives one user per Google account.
sonnet.q11: The user is redirected to the start (origin) with 'We couldn't complete sign-in with Google. Please try again.' There is no retry of the exchange: the state is already consumed, so the user must start again. Nothing changes and no session is created.
sonnet.q12: The origin (login or settings) is stored in Redis in the g:state record at start, never read from the callback URL. For settings, the record also stores the signed-in user_id, and the callback requires the current session user to equal it; otherwise error page. The link is then inserted for that user.
